name: Delaja
title: Priest and official in Judah
summary: Delaja is a name mentioned several places in the Old Testament. The most prominent Delaja was the son of Shemaiah, one of the leaders at King Jehoiakim's court who tried to prevent the king from burning the scroll of the prophet Jeremiah. Another Delaja was a priest in David's time who received the 23rd lot in the distribution of priestly duties.

keyEvents.title: Priestly division under David
keyEvents.description: A Delaja, son of Elhoenai, is mentioned in the Books of Chronicles as part of David's descendants. Another Delaja received the 23rd lot in the distribution of priestly duties during David's time.

keyEvents.title: The warning against burning the scroll
keyEvents.description: Delaja, son of Shemaiah, was among the officials who asked King Jehoiakim not to burn Jeremiah's scroll, but the king did not listen to them.

keyEvents.title: The scroll is read to the leaders
keyEvents.description: After Baruch had read Jeremiah's prophecies aloud, the contents were reported to Delaiah and the other officials who were sitting in the scribe's chamber in the king's palace.

keyEvents.title: The Officials' Reaction to the Prophecies
keyEvents.description: When Delaiah and the other leaders heard all the words from the scroll, they looked at each other with fear and told the king about its contents.

keyEvents.title: Descendants Who Returned from Exile
keyEvents.description: Delaiah's descendants are mentioned among those who returned from the Babylonian exile but could not prove their Israelite ancestry.
